I'm TJ Murphy, a Seattle artist. I started painting in 2020, following a desire to capture the light and color I kept noticing around me. That practice has grown into watercolor landscapes, portraits, and murals.

Natural beauty and the freedom to choose our own path run through the work. This page is where I'll share the paintings, the process, and the places and people behind them.

What would you like to see more of: landscapes, portraits, or murals?

https://vermillionaurora.com/links/?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=artist_launch_oct_2026&utm_content=meet-tj

How much color can come from a small palette?

For my watercolor pastel portraits, I usually begin with three primaries and a dark tone. Changing those primaries changes the possibilities of the whole painting. I love the deep saturation and the way pigment settles into the paper.

This is Girl Tuning Guitar. The quiet attention of the subject gives the color somewhere to go.

Would you like a closer look at this technique?

https://vermillionaurora.com/products/painting-guitarist/?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=artist_launch_oct_2026&utm_content=limited-palette

El Zonte at Dawn, El Salvador.

A shoreline gives light somewhere to gather: across the sky, across the water, and along the breaking waves. In this watercolor pastel, color carries the atmosphere.

Fine-art prints are available through my website. Open the painting page to see the current size, paper, and framing options. If you have a wall in mind, start with its measurements.

https://vermillionaurora.com/products/painting-shoreline-at-dusk/?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=artist_launch_oct_2026&utm_content=shore-print

Sunset on Sucia Island in Puget Sound.

Sometimes the dark shapes are what make the light visible. Here, the shoreline and silhouettes hold the sunset's color. Painting gives me a way to keep paying attention to that relationship.

The original has sold, but it remains part of the collection and the story of the work. What place keeps pulling you back to look again?

https://vermillionaurora.com/products/painting-sunset-silhouette/?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=artist_launch_oct_2026&utm_content=sucia-light

A closer way to look at El Zonte at Dawn: follow the painting from the bright horizon down into the waves.

The sky and water have different rhythms. One opens outward; the other breaks into repeated marks. I enjoy what happens when those rhythms meet in watercolor pastel.

Where does your eye settle first: the light on the horizon or the water in the foreground?

https://vermillionaurora.com/products/painting-shoreline-at-dusk/?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=artist_launch_oct_2026&utm_content=shore-composition

Some places deserve a painting of their own.

This garden mural brings together a cormorant, Puget Sound, the Olympic Mountains, and sunset color. A commission can begin with a place you return to, a view from home, or a landscape that carries a memory.

If you have a place in mind, tell me about it. Share a reference image, your preferred size, and any colors you'd like to explore through the commission form.

https://vermillionaurora.com/?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=artist_launch_oct_2026&utm_content=place-commission#contact

MJ Spinning at Chalet.

Portraiture is a way to pay attention to someone: their expression, their energy, and the details that make them recognizable. In this watercolor pastel, headphones and a slight smile carry part of that story.

Music and painting both leave room for feeling that doesn't need a full explanation. What detail in a portrait makes a person feel present to you?

https://vermillionaurora.com/products/painting-portrait-in-blue-light/?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=artist_launch_oct_2026&utm_content=music-portrait

A portrait can hold more than one person's likeness. It can hold the space between people: a glance, laughter, or the way they lean toward one another.

In watercolor, I enjoy letting those expressions share the page with lively color and the texture of the paper. The picture can feel alive without every detail being spelled out.

Would you choose a quiet portrait or an animated moment like this one?

https://vermillionaurora.com/about/?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=artist_launch_oct_2026&utm_content=shared-expression

A portrait commission starts with someone who matters to you.

It could be one person, a couple, or a shared moment. My watercolor pastel approach uses a limited palette to explore expression, saturated color, and the texture of the paper. Girl Tuning Guitar offers a glimpse of that approach.

Tell me who you'd like painted and what you want the portrait to hold. The commission form accepts an optional reference image, desired size, and palette swatch.

https://vermillionaurora.com/?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=artist_launch_oct_2026&utm_content=portrait-commission#contact

A garden can have a window into another landscape.

For this mural, I brought together a cormorant on a piling, sunset over Puget Sound, the Olympic Mountains, and sailboats. The painting also needed to belong among the plants around it.

Working at mural scale changes the relationship between a picture and its setting. Where would you put a painted view: a garden, a room, or a shared public space?

https://vermillionaurora.com/murals/?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=artist_launch_oct_2026&utm_content=garden-mural#garden

Berlín, El Salvador: a mural becomes part of the everyday life around it.

The finished sign sits beside a basketball court. People, play, and a place's identity meet in the same scene. This is one of the things I value about mural work: a painting can live where a community gathers.

Natural beauty and self-sovereignty are threads through my practice, alongside the people who give a place its character. Explore this project and its photographs on the site.

https://vermillionaurora.com/murals/berlin-el-salvador/?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=artist_launch_oct_2026&utm_content=berlin-community

Have a wall, garden, or shared space that could use a painting?

I work on murals as well as watercolor portraits and landscapes. A mural project begins with the setting, the people who use it, and the feeling you want the space to carry. This garden piece offers one example.

Send me a photograph of the space, its approximate dimensions, and your idea through the commission form. We can start a conversation about what belongs there.

https://vermillionaurora.com/?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=artist_launch_oct_2026&utm_content=mural-commission#contact
